title: Resolve every cited page to its id
statement: Before acting on feedback, resolve each page it cites to the page's stable id, from its link or by matching its on-screen text, since delivery surfaces number pages differently.
example: An old link to page 5 opens the page whose id is p4, because the count includes an opening video.
detail: A reading course delivers each lesson on two surfaces that name the same page differently. On one, a page's address is its authored id, but old links that give a page number still resolve by position, so `?page=5` lands on `/p4`, the fifth page counting the opening video (`grade3-reading/.claude/skills/reviewer-round/SKILL.md`, lines 25-29); the other prepends a welcome page and one page per unit film on a unit's first lesson, so its 'page 3' is often the lesson's first page (lines 30-36). The course's procedure for taking in feedback therefore resolves every cited link or screenshot to the lesson and page id before registering it, matches a screenshot's on-screen text into the lesson's data when there is no link, and records both forms and which surface the feedback came from (lines 19-23 and 35-44).

evidence.quote: the book's "page 3" is often the lesson's p0 — NEVER count dots or "page N" words from a reviewer; resolve to the id in the URL bar or, for a screenshot with no URL, match the on-screen text into the lesson JSON

Legacy ?page=<n> still resolves, by POSITION, into the path form (verified live: ?page=5 lands on /p4, the 5th page counting the video opener p0) — so a ?page=N link in old feedback is a position, not an id.
A reviewer phrase like "the vocab page" or "page 5 of 13" is AMBIGUOUS across surfaces
Resolve each cited link/screenshot to `lessonId + page id` before registering, and record BOTH forms in the register row
